ownerPhrases.question: For 'He gave food to that person', should we use Temov?
ownerPhrases.interpretation: Owner confirmed using Temov for the 'he gave' sentence as prompted.
ownerPhrases.note: Earlier example also uses Temov with an English 'they' prompt; do not infer exclusive singular meaning.

ownerPhrases.englishPrompt: She gave food to that person.
ownerPhrases.kashmiriExact: تٔمۍ دِژ أمِس شخصس کینہہ کھیٛن۔
ownerPhrases.mappingNote: Mapped by order of the three following sentences; user did not number these three individually.

ownerPhrases.englishPrompt: He did not give food to that person.
ownerPhrases.kashmiriExact: تٔمۍ دِژ نہٕ أمِس شخصس کانٛہہ کھیٛن۔
ownerPhrases.mappingNote: English subject is he, but Kashmiri subject and verb forms match the preceding 'She gave' example: do not treat the gender distinction as validated. Request clarification later.

ownerPhrases.englishPrompt: She did not say anything to me.
ownerPhrases.mappingNote: Compare with Lesson 2 positive 'She said to me': تٔمۍ ووٚن مےٚ.

observations: Temov explicitly accepted for he gave; also present in an earlier sentence labelled they gave, so its scope remains unresolved.
The food-giving negative includes نہٕ, and the food word changes from کینہہ to کانٛہہ. Avoid claiming negation is the only difference.
She said to me versus She did not say anything to me supports the phrase ووٚن نہٕ and کیٚنٛہہ in that context.
The direct negative food answer cannot by itself confirm third-person masculine because the supplied verb/subject match the feminine-labeled example.
pendingQuestions: Confirm whether the food sentence written under 'He did not give' intentionally uses تٔمۍ دِژ or was intended as 'She did not give'.
Determine case and gender variation in gave/gave not; isolate forms through more minimal pairs.
Validate Perso-Arabic orthography only as user explicitly supplies or approves it.
policy: Preserve all exact strings and mark mapping/grammar uncertainty; not a Hadith translation approval.
